issues: Scanner test never asserts the sha256 of a regular file. rows[0] (CACHEDIR.TAG, content 'wrong') only has bytes checked; sha256 is unasserted, and the final refuse() passes regardless of hash value. A collect() mutant that emits sha256:null (or hashes the wrong content/path) for files passes the oracle, so the 'sha256:file hash' contract clause is untested. Add assert.equal(rows[0].sha256, createHash('sha256').update('wrong').digest('hex')).

Accessor rejection is only exercised on the top-level object ({get hidden()}). No test defines a getter on an entry (e.g. Object.defineProperty(input.hidden[0],'bytes',{get(){reads++;return 10}})) or on the arrays, so 'reject accessors before property reads' is unverified for nested data; an implementation that reads entry fields directly would pass.

Traversal root is only implicit: the test relies on 'outside/' at importedRoot never appearing in rows, i.e. collect must scan frozenPackage only, but the contract text only says 'read-only fs traversal'. If the intended root were importedRoot the deepEqual would fail for a correct implementation; the contract should state the traversal root explicitly.
